key_insight: Higher-Order Grammar Representation (HGR) converts molecules with ring and motif topology into compact grammar rule sequences, making higher-order structure usable by standard sequence models while preserving expressiveness.
engineering_relevance: HGR offers a practical, scalable representation for molecular generative and foundation models that improves validity, distribution matching, and downstream prediction across multiple benchmarks.
method: Lift molecules to combinatorial complexes to explicitly capture higher-order topology.
Parse each complex into a sequence of production rules under a context-free higher-order grammar.
Use the resulting sequence representation for both generation and transferable representation learning.
evidence_signal: The paper reports 100% validity by construction and first-place FCD on all five generation benchmarks, plus the best mean AUC across seven MoleculeNet tasks with gains of 8.3 and 3.3 points over the strongest baseline under probing and full fine-tuning.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the higher-order grammar and benchmark coverage; constructing and decoding these representations may be less straightforward for novel chemistries or very large molecular systems.
paper_title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
